relevance_note: Case report of a boy and his younger brother with recurrent pyogenic arthritis in whom genetic testing found a PSTPIP1 variant: "Genetic testing indicated the presence of proline-serine-threonine phosphatase interacting protein 1 gene mutation in both boys."
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; the JSON was assembled with a short Python script in the scratch directory and every span was checked verbatim against the paper by script. Four people: the proband ('patient', rule 5), his younger brother, his asymptomatic carrier father, and his grandfather (recurrent pyoderma, declined genetic testing; side of the family not stated, so no inheritance link from him). Variants: the paper states the patient, brother and father 'were all heterozygous for the PSTPIP1 gene mutation ... (c.36+68 G>A, c.137+47 G>C, and c.562+114C>G het)'. The authors say the first and second sites 'were highly expressed in the sequencing of 1000 normal subjects' and single out only the third as 'a possible deleterious mutated site'; c.36+68 G>A and c.137+47 G>C were therefore treated as common variants the authors dismiss and left out of the variants table (judgment call; not explicitly called benign). Only c.562+114C>G was recorded, one row each for the patient, brother and father. The paper says the variants were 'found in the exon region' while the printed notation has intronic offsets; recorded as printed, variant type left 'not reported'. Inheritance 'inherited paternal' for both boys because the paper states their father carries the same mutation; mother never mentioned. The brother's exclusions of fever, acne and pyoderma gangrenosum rest on 'his younger brother presented in the same way' following the patient's 'no fever, acne, or pyoderma gangrenosum'. The grandfather's 'recurrent pyoderma' was not equated with pyoderma gangrenosum (checklist left not reported). The father's 'no symptoms' / 'never showed signs of the syndrome' was recorded as one excluded feature and not used to exclude specific checklist items. 'Liver and kidney function showed no obvious abnormality' was recorded as excluded abnormal liver/kidney function only; it does not exclude the composite kidney-involvement checklist item. The peri-knee abscess resected at surgery was counted as a soft-tissue abscess for the checklist. Age 7 is the age at admission/report; no age at onset or diagnosis is stated. n_patients_reported = 2 from 'both boys' (the father is a carrier, not a patient). No contradictions found.

treatment_summary.value: two knee surgeries (arthroscopic knee debridement and peri-knee abscess resection) followed by vancomycin and rifampicin; after diagnosis naproxen, high-dose prednisone and methotrexate with poor efficacy; switched to intravenous tocilizumab 8 mg/kg every 4 weeks (four treatments), with no suppurative arthritis during treatment and CRP, PCT and IL-6 restored or nearly normal
span: The boy underwent arthroscopic knee debridement and peri-knee abscess resection. He was treated with vancomycin and rifampicin after each operation
the boy was treated with naproxen (0.2 g per time, four times a day), high-dose prednisone (1–2 mg/kg/day), and methotrexate (10 mg/m^2/week)
due to poor efficacy of the medication combination and elevation of IL-6, we switched to intravenous infusion of tocilizumab once every 4 weeks at a dose of 8 mg/kg
The boy had received four treatments with tocilizumab and did not develop suppurative arthritis for the duration of treatment.
The CRP (27.40 mg/L), PCT (0.04 ng/mL), and IL-6 (23.88 pg/mL) levels were restored or nearly normal.
